topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of complement and frames its importance and complexity within immunology.

topics.label: Foundational Concepts and Organization of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the overall architecture, nomenclature conventions, and central biochemical role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways recognize targets and reach the trigger threshold for C3 convertase activity.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream immune functions executed once complement is activated, including opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory mechanisms and surface factors that prevent complement from destroying healthy host cells.

topics.label: Clinical Consequences of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the distinct clinical manifestations and disease risks resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components and regulators.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the molecular strategies that pathogens employ to subvert and survive complement attack.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the discussion of complement and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
